cards.title: Semimechanistic Model Structure for Biphasic Killing
cards.claim: Biphasic time-kill curves (rapid initial killing followed by reduced killing rate) are effectively modeled by dividing the total bacterial population into two subpopulations: a growing drug-susceptible population and a resting insusceptible (persister) population. The drug effect is modeled as an increase in the killing rate of the susceptible state, often using an Emax model. This structure accounts for phenotypic switching rather than assuming a single homogeneous population.
conditions: Applicable when time-kill data shows a decline in killing rate over time not explained by drug degradation.
Requires frequent sampling to distinguish growth phases.
In vitro static or dynamic models; does not automatically imply in vivo efficacy.
required_inputs: Time-series CFU/ml data for control and treatment groups.
Measured drug concentration-time profiles (if dynamic model) or constant concentrations (if static).
MIC values for the specific strain/drug pair.
limitations: The 'persister' state is a phenotypic model construct; it does not prove genetic resistance.
Model predictability is limited to conditions similar to those studied.
Does not account for immune defense or host factors.
cards.downstream_use: Use this structure to fit PK/PD models for drugs exhibiting biphasic killing. Do not assume this structure applies to drugs with monophasic killing or different resistance mechanisms without validation.
cards.retrieval_keywords: Time-kill, regrowth and resistance mechanism interpretation

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
